We demonstrate how automatic differentiation, validated against hand-derived analytical functional derivatives and finite differences, enables inverse modeling over millions of parameters and allows for sensitivity and stability analysis as well as correct eigenmode initialization. The differentiability of astronomix furthermore enables training machine-learning models inside the simulator. On a single GPU at a given resolution, astronomix has runtimes of the same order of magnitude as the GPU-optimized code AthenaPK but reaches far lower errors on smooth problems due to its higher order. astronomix scales to multiple GPUs ($\sim 6.5$ strong scaling speedup on $8$ GPUs) and multiple nodes ($\sim 76\%$ weak scaling efficiency on $16$ GPUs over $4$ nodes). We also present a novel fourth-order self-gravity scheme which complements the fifth-order finite difference constrained transport magnetohydrodynamics scheme implemented in astronomix. To maximize performance, we created an agentic skill that generates and validates custom Pallas GPU kernels from our JAX reference code and test suite. The simulator is available at https://github.com/leo1200/astronomix.

AI.tldr: astronomix is a performant differentiable hydrodynamics simulator in Python/JAX, allowing for inverse modeling and machine-learning training, achieving high accuracy and efficiency on GPUs.
AI.motivation: The need for a high-performance, differentiable hydrodynamics simulator that facilitates inverse modeling, sensitivity analysis, and integration with machine-learning techniques.
AI.method: Developed using Python/JAX with automatic differentiation for parameter analysis, validated against analytical models. Features a fourth-order self-gravity scheme and custom GPU kernel generation for performance optimization.
AI.result: astronomix delivers competitive runtimes comparable to GPU-optimized AthenaPK while minimizing errors on smooth problems, achieving significant scalability improvements across multiple GPUs and nodes.
AI.conclusion: The simulator not only enhances computational efficiency for hydrodynamic simulations but also integrates advanced machine-learning capabilities, making it a valuable tool for researchers in the field.

title: Could $\barΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ form bound hadronic molecule with explicit $P-wave$ ?
summary: In this article, the explicit $P-wave$ of the $\barΛ_cΛ_c$ dibaryon states with the $J^{PC}=0^{-\pm}$ and $1^{-\pm}$ are studied via twelve interpolated currents. Results show that the positive and negative charge conjugations for the studied states do not have too much difference, the contribution of the gluon from covariant derivative of the current with $P-wave$ could be neglected. The numerical results of the masses of the $P-wave$ $\barΛ_cΛ_c$ are high above the threshold of the two $\barΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ baryon constituents, $\barΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ are unlikely to form the bound molecules with explicit $P-wave$ . Pole residues of the related states are also calculated.

AI.tldr: The study investigates the $P-wave$ $ arΛ_cΛ_c$ dibaryon states with specific quantum numbers, finding no significant difference between charge conjugations and concluding that stable $P-wave$ states are unlikely due to mass results above the threshold.
AI.motivation: To explore the properties of P-wave $ arΛ_cΛ_c$ dibaryon states and understand their likelihood of forming bound states.
AI.method: The analysis is conducted through twelve interpolated currents to study the quantum states' properties and calculate their masses and pole residues.
AI.result: The mass results indicate that the $P-wave$ $ arΛ_cΛ_c$ states are significantly above the threshold for bound states, with negligible contributions from certain gluon interactions.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that stable bound $ arΛ_c$ and $Λ_c$ molecules in the $P-wave$ configuration are unlikely due to the high mass results.

title: Beyond Spin: QCD Magnetars
comment: 37 journal pages, 2 figures, 9 tables and 6 appendices
summary: We present a unified framework in which anomalous X-ray pulsars (AXPs), soft gamma-ray repeaters (SGRs), superluminous supernovae (SLSNe-I), luminous fast blue optical transients (LFBOTs), and fast radio bursts (FRBs) originate from quark deconfinement in the core of a massive neutron star (NS). Spontaneous ferromagnetism in the deconfined phase generates ~10^18 G core fields, producing a highly magnetized hybrid star (HS) - the "QCD magnetar" - whose surface field is set by NS mass, not birth spin. The Quark-Nova (QN) that forms the HS ejects ~0.01M_sun of neutron-rich outer layers, powering a kilonova and leaving the HS crustless for centuries. During this phase, magnetic instabilities at the hadron-quark interface release rising flux ropes that power X-ray-quiet FRBs; as the crust reforms, the source evolves into an X-ray-loud AXP&SGR. Two parameters govern the model: a critical mass M_dec triggering deconfinement, and a critical period P_fast separating fast and slow rotators. Fast rotators inject spin-down energy into the QN ejecta, producing an LFBOT - directly observable once the SN ejecta is optically thin, or via binary accretion with no preceding SN; otherwise the LFBOT is reprocessed by the SN ejecta into an SLSN-I. A Bayesian Monte Carlo population synthesis reproduces the observed rates of AXPs&SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs with M_dec ~2.1M_sun and P_fast ~5.5 ms, and predicts non-merger r-process signatures and kilonovae from isolated NSs, with or without an LFBOT. The QN ejecta also carries its own DM and RM, independent of environment, predicted to appear as excess dispersion and rotation measure in FRBs once Galactic, host, and intergalactic contributions are removed. These provide direct observational tests of the hadron-quark phase transition and ferromagnetic ordering in dense quark matter.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a framework linking various cosmic phenomena to quark deconfinement in neutron stars, introducing the concept of 'QCD magnetars' and explaining their evolution and observable signatures.
AI.motivation: To unify diverse astronomical observations like AXPs, SGRs, and FRBs under a single theoretical framework, enhancing understanding of their origins in neutron star physics.
AI.method: The authors develop a model based on quark deconfinement in neutron stars, involving spontaneous ferromagnetism and magnetic instabilities, using Bayesian Monte Carlo simulations for population synthesis.
AI.result: The model successfully reproduces observed rates of AXPs, SGRs, SLSNe-I, and LFBOTs, while predicting observable features like non-merger r-process signatures and excess dispersion in FRBs.
AI.conclusion: The findings support observational tests for the phase transition from hadronic to quark matter, and provide a comprehensive interpretation of several transient cosmic events.

title: The muon collider: expected physics, technological solutions, and the prospect of a 21 km ring at the UNK site
summary: A multi-TeV muon collider has emerged as one of the most compelling options for the post-LHC energy frontier. Because the muon is an elementary particle that radiates $\sim\!10^9$ times less synchrotron power than an electron of the same energy, a circular muon collider delivers the full beam energy to the hard collision in a remarkably compact ring, combining the energy reach of a $100$~TeV-class proton machine with the clean final states of a lepton collider. This review summarizes the expected physics results -- Higgs couplings and self-couplings, electroweak and vector-boson-fusion processes, the top quark, a broad beyond-the-Standard Model programme, and a near-complete closure of the thermal window for electroweak WIMP dark matter -- and the status of the enabling technologies, emphasizing for each challenge how it is being solved and where the solution is documented: muon production, ionization cooling (demonstrated in the transverse plane by MICE), rapid acceleration, high-field HTS magnets, the machine-detector interface, and the neutrino-flux constraint. Building on this foundation, this review examines the prospect of housing a muon collider in the existing 21~km UNK tunnel near Protvino, where the magnetic-rigidity relation maps realistic arc fields onto a centre-of-mass energy of order $10$-$20$ TeV -- reaching the IMCC 10~TeV reference with conventional dipoles and exceeding it with high-temperature-superconductor dipoles. It closes with a discussion of non-collider applications of the intense muon beams such a facility would develop -- muon-catalyzed fusion, muography, muonic-atom isotopic analysis, and muon spin spectroscopy -- several with a long tradition in the Russian physics institutes.

AI.tldr: This review discusses the potential of a multi-TeV muon collider as a future research facility, emphasizing its advantages over electron and proton colliders, outlining expected physics outcomes, technological challenges, and possible applications.
AI.motivation: The muon collider represents a compelling approach to explore new physics beyond the LHC, thanks to the muon's low synchrotron radiation loss which allows high-energy collisions in compact structures.
AI.method: The review evaluates the physics prospects and critical enabling technologies necessary for muon collider operation, such as muon production, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, and high-field magnets, alongside the proposed implementation in the UNK tunnel.
AI.result: The muon collider is projected to achieve centre-of-mass energies of approximately 10-20 TeV, potentially addressing significant open questions in particle physics and dark matter.
AI.conclusion: In addition to collider physics, muon beams could advance various applications including muon-catalyzed fusion, muography, and spectroscopy, leveraging established techniques in the field.

title: Time-dependent Accretion Disks in Tidal Disruption Events: Long-term Light Curves
summary: The time-dependent accretion disk has been applied to explain the light curves observed in tidal disruption events (TDEs). Radiation pressure instability is expected to be an important factor that can shape the evolution of the accretion disk. In this paper, we upgrade the time-dependent disk model in Guo $\&$ Qiao by incorporating an index $μ$ (with the stress tensor $\propto p^μp^{1-μ}_{\rm{gas}}$, where $p=p_{\rm{gas}} + p_{\rm{rad}}$) for the modified viscosity, and a parameter $f_{\rm{w}}$ for the strength of the wind. Meanwhile, we adopt a more realistic fallback rate to inject into the disk. After systematically testing the effects of the newly incorporated parameters, we find that $f_{\rm{w}}$ can affect the time when the instability occurs, while $μ$ can influence the occurrence and variation magnitude of the radiation pressure instability. When $μ<0.4$, the radiation pressure instability is completely removed from the disk, and the light curves evolve stably without large-scale magnitude variation. When $μ>0.4$, the light curves can show oscillations caused by the instability, or drop steeply when the instability occurs and become flat in the late-time evolution, which mainly occurs when the viscous viscosity parameter $α$ is small or the impact parameter $β$ is small. Since the drop magnitude can be modulated by $μ$, we apply these `decay-to-flatten' light curves to some optical/UV observations in TDEs with different magnitudes of decline. Finally, we discuss the potential application of our model to some special TDEs that show oscillations in the light curves.

AI.tldr: This paper enhances a time-dependent accretion disk model to explain light curves in tidal disruption events, focusing on the effects of radiation pressure instability and new parameters.
AI.motivation: To improve the understanding of light curves in tidal disruption events (TDEs) by incorporating significant factors affecting accretion disk dynamics.
AI.method: The study modifies a previous disk model by introducing parameters for viscosity and wind strength and applies a more realistic fallback rate to analyze their effects on radiation pressure instability.
AI.result: The analysis reveals that the wind strength $f_{\rm{w}}$ influences the timing of instability, while the viscosity index $μ$ determines the presence and magnitude of the radiation pressure instability, impacting the light curve behavior significantly.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model accounts for variations in light curves observed in TDEs, particularly the 'decay-to-flatten' behavior, and offers insights into special TDEs exhibiting oscillatory light curves.

title: Geometric Scaling and the Odderon
summary:
Based on geometric scaling of elastic $pp$ and possibly $p\bar{p}$ cross-sections, we derive simple formulae for
  the complex crossing-even and crossing-odd scattering amplitudes in terms of two interaction radii: $R(s)$ and $Q(s)$, respectively.
  Employing the COMPETE parametrization of the total cross-sections, we reproduce $ρ^{pp}$ and $ρ^{p\bar{p}}$ parameters with high
  accuracy, however we miss the 13~TeV TOTEM and ATLAS points. We show that a slight modification of the $p\bar{p}$ total cross-section
  corresponding to the Odderon, allows to accommodate $ρ^{pp}$ 13~TeV data.

AI.tldr: The paper presents formulas for elastic scattering amplitudes, deriving them from geometric scaling of cross-sections, and discusses the accuracy of reproducing specific parameters while addressing discrepancies with recent experimental data.
AI.motivation: The aim is to understand elastic scattering in high-energy proton-proton and proton-antiproton collisions using geometric scaling and interaction radii.
AI.method: The authors develop formulas for crossing-even and crossing-odd scattering amplitudes from elastic pp and p̄p cross-sections, using the COMPETE parametrization for total cross-sections.
AI.result: The derived formulas accurately reproduce the ρpp and ρp̄p parameters, although they do not align with certain 13 TeV TOTEM and ATLAS data points, which are reconciled by adjusting the p̄p total cross-section to involve the Odderon.
AI.conclusion: A revision of the p̄p cross-section, incorporating the Odderon effect, can lead to accurate predictions of the elastic scattering parameters at 13 TeV.

title: Black hole spin-mass correlation and vector resonant relaxation in gaseous star clusters: the origin of GW231123?
summary: During the formation of a star cluster a spin-mass correlation of stellar black holes is generated as they grow via accretion of the residual gas. Moreover, the black hole spin tends to be anti-aligned with its orbital angular momentum in the cluster. We show that GW231123, reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, lies on our predicted high-mass, high-spin plateau of the spin-mass correlation with positive Bayesian evidence over the LVK prior. Furthermore, vector resonant relaxation (VRR) equilibrium is favored over the isotropic LVK prior in reproducing the distribution of the relative spin tilt. The joint Bayes factor suggests strong evidence for the favored cluster models. GW231123 is thus consistent with our proposed channel that generates correlated black hole masses and spins, and drives the spins' orientations.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses the correlation between black hole spin and mass in star clusters, using the detection of GW231123 as validation for their model.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation mechanisms of stellar black holes and their spin-mass correlations during star cluster evolution.
AI.method: Analysis of GW231123 data relative to theoretical models predicting spin-mass correlations and spin orientations, particularly through vector resonant relaxation (VRR).
AI.result: GW231123 aligns with the predicted high-mass, high-spin plateau, with strong Bayesian evidence supporting the VRR scenario over the isotropic prior.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the hypothesis that correlated mass and spin of black holes result from cluster dynamics, with significant implications for understanding black hole formation.

title: Imprints of Higgs-portal fermionic dark matter on neutron-star tidal deformability and the mass-radius slope
summary: We investigate the structure of neutron stars (NSs) admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) using three density-dependent relativistic mean-field (DDRMF) functionals (DDME, DDB, and GDFM) for $β$-equilibrated nucleonic matter. Modeling DM as the lightest neutralino interacting via Higgs exchange, we treat the DM Fermi momentum $k_F^{\rm DM}$ as a control parameter in the range $0.02$-$0.06$ GeV. We solve the coupled mean-field and Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to obtain the mass-radius relation, maximum mass $M_{\rm max}$, radial sound speed profile $c_s^2$, and tidal deformability $Λ$. In all models, DM softens the equation of state, systematically reducing $M_{\rm max}$, the radius $R_{1.4}$ (at $1.4M_{\odot}$), and the tidal deformability $Λ_{1.4}$ (at $1.4M_{\odot}$) as $k_F^{\rm DM}$ increases. Consequently, the $2 M_\odot$ pulsar limit and NICER data place a model-dependent upper limit on the DM content, while the GW170817 tidal bound requires a minimal DM content for the stiffest functional. Using a recent Bayesian inference of the DDRMF equation of state as the nucleonic reference band, we evaluate if this DM imprint can be distinguished from nucleonic uncertainties using only measureable quantities. Analyzing the tidal deformability $Λ$ and mass-radius slope $dR/dM$ at fixed mass, we find that $Λ$ is a sharp discriminator: at $1.4 M_\odot$ and $k_F^{\rm DM}=0.06$ GeV, the DM-induced reduction of $Λ$ reaches $\simeq 8$ times the nucleonic $1σ$ width (model-independently $7.5$-$7.8σ$). The DM track leaves the nucleonic $1σ$ band for $k_F^{\rm DM}\gtrsim0.03$-$0.04$ GeV, whereas $dR/dM$ becomes diagnostic only for the heavier ($1.8$-$2.0 M_\odot$) branch.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how the presence of fermionic dark matter affects the structure and observable properties of neutron stars, particularly focusing on mass, radius, sound speed, and tidal deformability as functions of dark matter parameters.
AI.motivation: To understand the influence of fermionic dark matter on neutron star properties given the constraints from pulsar data and gravitational waves.
AI.method: The study employs density-dependent relativistic mean-field models and solves the coupled mean-field and Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to derive key relations and properties of neutron stars with dark matter.
AI.result: Dark matter softens the equation of state, leading to a decrease in maximum mass, radius, and tidal deformability as the dark matter Fermi momentum increases. A discernible link between dark matter presence and measurable quantities like tidal deformability is identified, allowing for discrimination from nucleonic uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that certain dark matter characteristics can be distinguished from nucleonic effects, particularly through the tidal deformability and mass-radius slope analysis.

title: The Complete Catalog of Gamma-Ray Transients Observed by GRBAlpha & VZLUSAT-2 CubeSat Missions
comment: submitted to The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, after revision
summary: We present the largest sample of gamma-ray transients observed by any CubeSat mission so far. Observations were acquired by a 1U CubeSat GRBAlpha, the smallest astrophysical space observatory, and a 3U CubeSat VZLUSAT-2. Both missions were technological pathfinders and carried a novel CsI scintillator-based detector read-out by silicon photomultipliers. They operated on Sun-synchronous low Earth orbits below 550 km for about four years; GRBAlpha between March 2021 and June 2025 while VZLUSAT-2 between January 2022 and November 2025. Despite being technological experiments, they observed over 300 gamma-ray transients including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), solar flares, soft gamma repeaters and one outburst from an X-ray binary. Among these are the two brightest GRBs ever observed, GRB 221009A and GRB 230307A, without saturation and GRBs at redshifts up to z=4.2. GRBAlpha also contributed to the InterPlanetary Network. Regular monitoring of transients was demonstrated by a detection rate of two transients or one GRB a week and the shortest time between two subsequent detections of only 42 minutes. We show that a constellation of nanosatellites around the Earth would observe at least 60% of Fermi/GBM GRBs with 5$σ$ significance and over 90% at 3$σ$ level. GRBAlpha and VZLUSAT-2 prove that routine monitoring of the gamma-ray sky can also be done by low-cost and quickly developed nanosatellite missions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents gamma-ray observations from two CubeSat missions, GRBAlpha and VZLUSAT-2, noting their success in detecting a significant number of gamma-ray transients.
AI.motivation: The study aims to showcase the capabilities of CubeSats in monitoring gamma-ray transients and contribute to the field of astrophysics.
AI.method: Using a novel CsI scintillator-based detector with silicon photomultipliers, GRBAlpha and VZLUSAT-2 operated in low Earth orbits to observe gamma-ray emissions over several years.
AI.result: The missions detected over 300 transients, including the brightest GRBs and established a detection rate of roughly two transients per week.
AI.conclusion: The successful operation of these low-cost nanosatellites demonstrates their potential for continuous gamma-ray sky monitoring.

title: Neutrino lines and photon continua from cascade dark matter decay
summary: We investigate the two-body decay of fermionic dark matter, $χ(\barχ)\to X+ν(\barν)$, where the light mediator $X$ subsequently decays into photons. We consider two benchmark models: an axion-like particle with $a\toγγ$, and a kinetically mixed dark vector with $A'\to3γ$. This decay topology produces a monochromatic neutrino line from the primary decay together with a broad secondary photon continuum. A key feature of the scenario is that the photon signal depends on the mediator decay length, whereas the neutrino line is produced promptly and is insensitive to the subsequent propagation of $X$. We derive dark matter lifetime limits from current and projected MeV gamma-ray and neutrino searches, including both Galactic and delayed extragalactic photon contributions. We find that photon constraints generally dominate for short-lived mediators, while neutrino-line searches can become competitive or provide the leading sensitivity in regions where mediator propagation substantially suppresses the photon signal. This conclusion remains stable under conservative extragalactic-only limits and a simplified treatment of Galactic spatial smearing.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes the two-body decay of fermionic dark matter into neutrinos and a mediator that decays into photons, highlighting the dependencies of photon and neutrino signals on the properties of the mediator.
AI.motivation: To explore the decay processes of dark matter and their implications for neutrino and photon signals, enhancing understanding of dark matter properties and guiding future searches.
AI.method: The authors examine two models, analyzing decay scenarios where dark matter decays directly into neutrinos and mediators that subsequently decay into photons, deriving limits on dark matter lifetimes based on existing and future gamma-ray and neutrino data.
AI.result: Photon emission is dominant for short-lived mediators, while neutrino line searches can provide competitive sensitivity in cases where photon signals are suppressed due to mediator propagation effects.
AI.conclusion: The study emphasizes the importance of both photon and neutrino signals in constraining dark matter properties, noting that different mediator behaviors impact the signals significantly.

title: Quantifying the Information Gain from Future High-Precision Radius Measurements for Identifying Twin Neutron Stars
summary: Twin neutron stars (NSs), characterized by identical gravitational masses but different radii, are among the most promising astrophysical signatures of a strong first-order hadron--quark phase transition in supradense matter. We investigate how increasingly precise NS radius measurements improve the Bayesian inference of twin-star observability using mock radius data for a canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NS. Radius uncertainties are varied from the current level of about $0.9$ km to the $\approx 0.1$ km precision anticipated from future X-ray and gravitational-wave observations. We quantify the information gained using the posterior distribution of the maximum twin-star radius separation $ΔR$ together with an analytical model of branch distinguishability and complementary information-theoretic measures based on the branch observational efficiency and the Shannon entropy. The combined analyses reveal three inference regimes: a prior-dominated regime for $σ_R \gtrsim 0.6$ km, a rapid information-gain regime for $0.2 \lesssim σ_R \lesssim 0.6$ km, and an information-saturation regime for $σ_R \lesssim 0.2$ km. These complementary analyses consistently indicate that radius measurements with a precision of about $0.2$ km already extract most of the information available for identifying twin NSs within the present Bayesian framework. Beyond establishing a quantitative observational benchmark for future high-precision radius measurements, this work provides a general Bayesian framework for quantifying the information gain from progressively more precise observations and identifying the point of diminishing scientific returns.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes how improved measurements of neutron star radii enhance the Bayesian inference for detecting twin neutron stars, demonstrating distinct information gain regimes based on measurement precision.
AI.motivation: To understand how precise radius measurements of neutron stars can help identify twin neutron stars and the phase transition in dense matter.
AI.method: Mock radius data for a canonical 1.4 solar mass neutron star is analyzed with varying uncertainties, employing Bayesian inference and information-theoretic measures.
AI.result: Three inference regimes are identified based on radius uncertainties, indicating that precision of about 0.2 km is largely sufficient for characterizing twin neutron stars.
AI.conclusion: The research establishes benchmarks for future high-precision measurements and offers a Bayesian framework to evaluate the information gain from observations.

title: Holographic spectral functions of exotic spin-1 mesons
summary: We develop a general holographic framework for computing thermal spectral functions of exotic spin--1 mesons. A bulk Proca mass encodes the canonical ultraviolet dimension of the interpolating operator, allowing channels with different ultraviolet scaling to be treated within a unified membrane-flow formalism in the zero-spatial-momentum limit. We test this framework in a soft-wall model with a gluon-condensate background for the hybrid $π_1$ and tetraquark-like $Z_c$ channels. The results show that dissociation temperatures of both channels lie below the phase transition temperatures. Increasing $c$ delays dissociation in both channels, but through different effects: both the vacuum-mass shift and thermal spectral deformation contribute in the $π_1$ channel, whereas the latter dominates in the $Z_c$ channel. Nevertheless, for the same environment, the $Z_c$ resonance dissociates at a lower temperature than the $π_1$ resonance.

AI.tldr: A holographic framework is devised to compute thermal spectral functions for exotic spin-1 mesons, revealing key differences in dissociation temperatures and behavior between the hybrid $π_1$ and tetraquark-like $Z_c$ channels.
AI.motivation: To present a unified approach for calculating thermal spectral functions of exotic mesons with varying ultraviolet scaling in a consistent manner.
AI.method: Utilizing a bulk Proca mass within a holographic model to analyze species like the hybrid $π_1$ and tetraquark-like $Z_c$ mesons in a soft-wall model under a gluon-condensate background.
AI.result: Dissociation temperatures for the $π_1$ and $Z_c$ channels are below the phase transition temperatures; increasing a parameter $c$ affects dissociation differently across the channels.
AI.conclusion: Despite differing responses to parameter changes, the $Z_c$ resonance consistently dissociates at lower temperatures than the $π_1$ resonance.

title: Detailed study of the dual symmetry of dense quark matter within the effective action formalism
comment: 17 pages; submitted to Chinese Physics C
summary: The symmetry properties of the phase diagram of dense quark matter composed of $u$ and $d$ quarks with three colors have been investigated in the framework of massless (3+1)-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) and QCD models. It turns out that in the presence of baryon $μ_B$, isospin $μ_I$, chiral $μ_5$ and chiral isospin $μ_{I5}$ chemical potentials, the Lagrangians of these models are invariant under the so-called dual transformation ${\cal D}$. In this paper, it has been shown that the path integration measure of the corresponding partition functions is also invariant under ${\cal D}$. Consequently, the entire NJL model (or QCD) thermodynamic potentials are dually symmetric. In particular, it means that in the total $(μ_B,μ_I,μ_5,μ_{I5})$-phase portraits of these models the chiral symmetry breaking (CSB) and charged pion condensation (PC) phases are arranged dually conjugate (or symmetrically) to each other. Dual symmetry between CSB and charged PC phases of quark matter is a fundamental property of massless dense QCD; it should be observed in the framework of any approximation to the QCD phase diagram, and have important implications for studies of the phase structure.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the dual symmetry properties of the phase diagram for dense quark matter with u and d quarks, demonstrating dually symmetric arrangements of chiral symmetry breaking and charged pion condensation phases under certain chemical potentials.
AI.motivation: To explore the symmetry properties within the phase diagram of dense quark matter, particularly in regards to chiral symmetry breaking and its implications.
AI.method: Analysis conducted within the framework of massless Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and QCD models, examining the invariance of Lagrangians and partition functions under dual transformation ${	extcal{D}}$.
AI.result: Demonstrated that the path integration measure of partition functions and the corresponding thermodynamic potentials are invariant under the dual transformation, establishing a dual symmetry between chiral symmetry breaking and charged pion condensation phases.
AI.conclusion: The chiral symmetry breaking and charged pion condensation phases are arranged symmetrically in the $(μ_B,μ_I,μ_5,μ_{I5})$-phase portraits, signifying a fundamental property of massless dense QCD that carries important implications for understanding the phase structure.

title: Scrutinizing lepton flavor universality and transition form factor correlation from charmed meson semileptonic decay into light strange vector $K^*$ meson
summary: In this paper, we calculate the transition form factors (TFFs) $A_{1,2}(q^2)$ and $V(q^2)$ of $D_s^+ \to K^{*0}$ decays by using the QCD light-cone sum rule (QCD LCSR) and constructing a correlation function containing the usual current, in which the twist-2 transverse and longitudinal light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) $φ^λ_{2;K^{*0}}(x,μ_0)$ with $λ=(\bot,\|)$ of the $K^{*0}$ meson constitute the main source of theoretical uncertainty. Based on this, we construct these LCDAs using the light-cone harmonic oscillator model. Subsequently, the TFFs obtained in the large recoil region are $A_{1}(0)=0.579_{-0.028}^{+0.024}$, $A_{2}(0)=0.414_{-0.023}^{+0.021}$, and $V(0)=0.830_{-0.020}^{+0.020}$, and the corresponding ratios are obtained to be $r_V=1.433_{-0.090}^{+0.110}$ and $r_2=0.715_{-0.067}^{+0.075}$. Furthermore, we predict the correlation of TFFs and their corresponding ratios. Then, we extrapolate the TFFs over the whole physical $q^2$-region and calculate the decay widths and branching fractions for the semileptonic decays $D_s^+\to K^{*0}\ell^+ν_{\ell}$. The results are $\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to K^{*0}e^+ν_{e})=(2.05_{-0.16}^{+0.13})\times 10^{-3}$ and $\mathcal{B}(D_s^+\to K^{*0}μ^+ν_μ)=(1.95_{-0.15}^{+0.13})\times 10^{-3}$. Meanwhile, we calculated the branching fraction ratio $\mathcal{R}_{μ/e}^{K^{*0}}$ to be $0.950_{-0.002}^{+0.004}$. In addition, we extract values of the CKM matrix element, obtaining $|V_{cd}|_{(e\text{-Channel})} = 0.225_{-0.005}^{+0.005}$ and $|V_{cd}|_{(μ\text{-Channel})} = 0.227_{-0.004}^{+0.011}$. Finally, we calculated the forward-backward asymmetry parameters for the $D_s^+\to K^{*0} \ell^+ν_{\ell}$ decay.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the transition form factors for $D_s^+ \to K^{*0}$ decays using QCD light-cone sum rules, assesses uncertainties from light-cone distribution amplitudes, and provides branching fractions and CKM matrix elements.
AI.motivation: To understand the decay processes of $D_s^+ \to K^{*0}$ and extract relevant physical parameters such as transition form factors and CKM matrix elements.
AI.method: The authors employ QCD light-cone sum rules to calculate transition form factors, constructing relevant light-cone distribution amplitudes through a harmonic oscillator model, and extrapolate results across the physical $q^2$-region.
AI.result: The calculated transition form factors are $A_{1}(0)=0.579$, $A_{2}(0)=0.414$, and $V(0)=0.830$. Branching fractions for $D_s^+\to K^{*0}e^+ν_{e}$ and $D_s^+\to K^{*0}μ^+ν_μ$ are roughly $2.05 \times 10^{-3}$ and $1.95 \times 10^{-3}$, respectively, with a ratio of $0.950$. Extraction of the CKM matrix element values yields $|V_{cd}|_{(e	ext{-Channel})} = 0.225$ and $|V_{cd}|_{(μ	ext{-Channel})} = 0.227$.
AI.conclusion: The study provides significant insight into $D_s^+ \to K^{*0}$ decays, presenting important measurements for transition form factors and CKM matrix elements, alongside forward-backward asymmetry parameters.

title: Breaking the Democratic Limit in the Generalized Friedberg-Lee Model: Implications for Neutrino Masses and Mixing
summary: We investigate a generalized Friedberg--Lee (FL) framework for neutrino masses, focusing on the singular parameter space at Point D ($α= β= -1/3$). At this limit, the neutrino mass matrix exhibits a democratic texture governed by the $S_3$ permutation symmetry. Although theoretically profound, the exact democratic limit is phenomenologically excluded as it predicts a degenerate mass spectrum and a vanishing reactor angle ($θ_{13}=0$). To reconcile this high-symmetry limit with experimental observations, we introduce a minimal and systematic perturbation that preserves the Twisted Friedberg--Lee (TFL) symmetry. This mechanism effectively lifts the mass degeneracy and breaks the magic and $μ$--$τ$ symmetries in a controlled manner. Our derivation avoids \textit{ad hoc} parameters, establishing a robust framework that yields a realistic inverted mass hierarchy ($m_3=0$), a non-zero $θ_{13}$, and intrinsic CP violation. We demonstrate that the model predicts maximal atmospheric mixing and a significant Dirac CP phase. The obtained numerical ranges for the neutrino masses and the Jarlskog invariant show excellent agreement with global fit data, providing a theoretically motivated foundation for neutrino flavor physics within the TFL scheme.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a modified Friedberg-Lee framework for neutrino masses at a specific point in parameter space, revealing implications for neutrino mass and mixing phenomena.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of the democratic neutrino mass matrix associated with theoretical perspectives and experimental data discrepancies.
AI.method: The authors propose a systematic perturbation that maintains symmetry while lifting mass degeneracy, enabling the model to adhere to observed phenomena in neutrino physics.
AI.result: The model successfully predicts a realistic inverted mass hierarchy, a non-zero reactor angle, maximal atmospheric mixing, and intrinsic CP violation, aligning with global fit data.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a robust theoretical framework that reconciles high-symmetry limits with experimental findings in neutrino flavor physics.

title: Kapitza Inspired Effective Interaction for the Exotic State X(3872): A Coupled-Channel Potential Model Study
summary: The X(3872) remains one of the most intriguing exotic hadrons, lying extremely close to the $D^0\bar{D}^{*0}$ threshold. We construct an effective potential consisting of Coulomb, linear confinement and a Kapitza-inspired term representing the averaged effect of fast gluonic fluctuations. Numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation shows that this term provides effective attraction in the intermediate-distance region, yielding a ground-state mass of $3871.7 \pm 0.9$ MeV in excellent agreement with experiment. Coupled-channel analysis indicates a dominant molecular component ($\sim 65\%-72\%$) with a significant compact tetraquark core ($\sim 28\%-35\%$). We also present predictions for low-lying excited states. The model offers a physically motivated mechanism for threshold tuning.

AI.tldr: The X(3872) is analyzed using an effective potential model, leading to a mass prediction consistent with experimental data and indicating a molecular structure with a tetraquark core.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature of the X(3872) exotic hadron and its properties near the $D^0 ar{D}^{*0}$ threshold.
AI.method: An effective potential is constructed including Coulomb and linear confinement terms, along with a Kapitza-inspired term for gluonic fluctuations, followed by numerical solutions of the Schrödinger equation.
AI.result: The analysis yields a ground-state mass of $3871.7 \, 	ext{MeV}$, consistent with experimental values, and identifies the X(3872) as having a molecular component (~65%-72%) and a tetraquark core (~28%-35%).
AI.conclusion: The model successfully explains the threshold behavior and predicts low-lying excited states.

title: Relativistic bound-state solutions for a non-central Schi{ö}berg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular terms
summary: Singular interactions can reshape quantum spectra by changing admissible wavefunction domains. In this study, we investigate this mechanism in the Klein--Gordon equation for a non-central Schiöberg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular barriers. Equal scalar and vector couplings separate the radial and angular dynamics. We solve the angular equation exactly and treat the radial equation with the Greene--Aldrich approximation, obtaining Jacobi-polynomial wavefunctions and an implicit relativistic quantization condition. The equatorial inverse-square singularity splits configuration space into reflection-related sectors with identical angular spectra. Reducing the barrier to zero within one sector retains only odd-parity states, unlike the regular full-domain problem, which restores both parities. The nonrelativistic limit recovers the Schr{ö}dinger spectrum. For NaH and Na$_2$, low-lying vibrational energies agree reasonably with experiment, whereas near-dissociation deviations reveal asymptotic limitations.

AI.tldr: This study explores how singular interactions affect quantum spectra by examining a specific potential in the Klein-Gordon equation, deriving wavefunctions and quantization conditions.
AI.motivation: To understand how singular interactions can influence quantum spectral properties by altering admissible wavefunction domains.
AI.method: The angular part of the Klein-Gordon equation is solved exactly, while the radial part is approached using the Greene-Aldrich approximation, yielding Jacobi-polynomial wavefunctions and an implicit relativistic quantization condition.
AI.result: The study reveals that an equatorial inverse-square singularity leads to reflection-related sectors with identical angular spectra and that reducing the barrier results in odd-parity states, contrasting with the full-domain problem which allows both parities.
AI.conclusion: The findings align low-lying vibrational energies for NaH and Na2 with experimental data, although discrepancies near dissociation highlight limits in the model.

title: Relative enhancement of low-mass vector-boson exchange in higher waves matrix elements: parity non-conservation in hydrogen
summary: Models of unification predict additional $Z'$ boson, which contributes to parity non-conservation (PNC) in atoms. If $Z'$ boson is light, ratio of $Z'$ boson contribution to the Standard Model $Z$ boson contribution to atomic PNC increases with decreasing nuclear charge $Z$ faster than $1/Z^2$. This motivated our previous study of PNC in hydrogen and deuterium proportional to the weak interaction matrix elements $<s|W|p> $. An enormous additional relative enhancement appears in the matrix elements between higher waves, such as $<p_{1/2,3/2} | W | d_{3/2,5/2}> $, since $p_{3/2}$ and $d_{3/2,5/2}$ wave functions vanish at $r \to 0$, suppressing matrix elements of the contact $Z$ boson mediated contact electron-nucleus interaction. Measurements of $<p_{1/2,3/2} | W | d_{3/2,5/2}> $ will simplify disentanglement of the $Z'$ contribution from the Standard Model background.

AI.tldr: This study focuses on the enhanced contributions of a predicted light $Z'$ boson to atomic parity non-conservation (PNC), particularly in hydrogen and deuterium, highlighting how this enhancement simplifies the separation of $Z'$ contributions from the Standard Model dynamics.
AI.motivation: The presence of a light $Z'$ boson, as predicted by unification models, necessitates a closer examination of its influence on PNC in atomic systems, particularly due to its potential dominance at low nuclear charges.
AI.method: The analysis investigates the weak interaction matrix elements $<s|W|p>$, calculating enhancements in specific higher wave matrix elements between atomic states, especially $<p_{1/2,3/2} | W | d_{3/2,5/2}>$.
AI.result: A significant relative enhancement in the matrix elements was found for higher wave states due to the zero values of certain wave functions at the origin, which reduces $Z$ boson contributions, making the separation of $Z'$ contributions more straightforward in experimental measurements.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate that measuring the targeted matrix elements can facilitate the disentanglement of $Z'$ contributions from the complexities of the Standard Model in atomic PNC experiments.

title: EPIC-CIM: Training Convolutional Neural Networks on a Coherent Ising Machine via Equilibrium Propagation
summary: Quantum convolutional neural networks, due to the involvement of quantum measurements and discrete quantum state evolution, face inherent training challenges associated with non-differentiable operations and discrete optimization dynamics, which make conventional gradient-based learning difficult to apply effectively. In this context, energy-based learning provides a promising alternative by reformulating network training as an energy minimization process without explicit gradient backpropagation.In this framework, input data are processed through convolutional operations, followed by quantum sampling to generate intermediate binary representations, while the output layer also relies on quantum sampling to produce final predictions. The overall network energy is composed of convolutional feature matching terms, linear coupling terms at the output layer, and global output constraint terms, enabling both parameter updates and feature evolution to be described through physically interpretable energy dynamics. Furthermore, under the equilibrium propagation mechanism, the energy difference between the free phase and the weakly clamped phase is exploited to drive parameter updates without explicit gradient computation, thereby enabling stable and consistent learning in non-differentiable and discrete spaces. While remaining consistent with classical convolutional learning theory, the proposed framework enhances interpretability and observability through quantum energy modeling, offering a unified physical perspective for efficient QCNN training and the integration of quantum computing with artificial intelligence.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an energy-based learning framework for training quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs), addressing challenges of non-differentiable training and enhancing interpretability through quantum energy dynamics.
AI.motivation: Given the inherent challenges in training QCNNs due to non-differentiable operations and discrete optimization, there's a need for an alternative learning approach that doesn't rely on conventional gradient backpropagation.
AI.method: The framework reformulates QCNN training as an energy minimization process, utilizing convolutional operations and quantum sampling for binary representations, along with energy dynamics for parameter updates and feature evolution.
AI.result: The method allows stable learning in non-differentiable spaces and aligns with classical convolutional learning theory, while increasing interpretability through quantum energy modeling.
AI.conclusion: This approach offers a cohesive physical perspective for effective QCNN training, bridging the gap between quantum computing and artificial intelligence.

title: Heavy quark mass dependence of the $Λ_Q$ light-cone distribution amplitude in QCD
summary: We study the heavy quark mass dependence of the leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) of the $Λ_Q$ baryon in QCD. Starting from the factorization formula that relates the QCD LCDA to the boosted heavy-quark effective theory (bHQET) LCDA, we derive a first-order partial differential equation governing this mass dependence in the peak region. The equation is solved analytically, and the explicit factor connecting LCDAs at different heavy quark masses is presented. We further incorporate Borel-resummed perturbative corrections from a renormalon model into the factorization. The impact of these renormalon corrections on the mass dependence is studied, and a numerical analysis using a simple LCDA model is performed to illustrate the behavior and to assess the uncertainties arising from the corrections, thereby providing a numerical estimate of the associated power corrections to the mass dependence. Our results provide an essential tool for extrapolating lattice QCD calculations of heavy-baryon LCDAs from smaller simulated masses to the physical bottom quark mass.

AI.tldr: The paper examines the heavy quark mass effect on the LCDAs of the $Λ_Q$ baryon, deriving a differential equation and including corrections to aid extrapolation in lattice QCD studies.
AI.motivation: Understanding the mass dependence of LCDAs in heavy baryons is crucial for precise lattice QCD predictions and connecting theoretical models with experimental results.
AI.method: A factorization approach connects QCD LCDA to bHQET LCDA, leading to a first-order differential equation which is solved analytically. Borel-resummed perturbative corrections are incorporated and numerically analyzed with a simple LCDA model.
AI.result: An explicit factor linking LCDAs at varying heavy quark masses is provided, alongside an assessment of uncertainties due to renormalon corrections.
AI.conclusion: The findings offer valuable insights for extrapolating lattice QCD results for heavy baryons to physical quark masses, enhancing the accuracy of theoretical predictions.

title: QR-SPPS: Quantum-Native Retail Supply Chain Risk Simulation via VQE, ADAPT-VQE Counterfactual Policy Ranking, and DOS-QPE Boltzmann Tail Risk Quantification
comment: 38 pages, 12 figures, 9 tables. Developed for the Fujitsu Quantum Simulator Challenge 2025-26. Source code and supplementary materials available upon request
summary: Classical supply chain risk models treat node failures as statistically independent events, systematically underestimating correlated cascade failures across multi-tier supplier networks. We present QR-SPPS (Quantum-Native Retail Shock Propagation and Policy Stress Simulator), a quantum-native framework for retail supply chain risk analysis implemented on the Qiskit ecosystem using OpenFermion-based Ising Hamiltonian encoding. A 40-node, four-tier supply network is mapped to a 40-qubit Hamiltonian with ZZ coupling terms representing correlated supplier dependencies. A hardware-efficient Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) computes the stress ground state, revealing entangled cascade failures that differ substantially from classical Monte Carlo predictions. We further introduce the application of ADAPT-VQE gradient screening for counterfactual policy evaluation, enabling real-time ranking of six crisis interventions without repeated variational optimization. Finally, Density-of-States Quantum Phase Estimation (DOS-QPE) reconstructs the eigenspectrum through Trotter evolution and estimates Boltzmann-weighted catastrophe probabilities as a function of market-volatility temperature, providing a quantum-native tail-risk metric compatible with Value-at-Risk analysis. The framework demonstrates scalable quantum algorithms for correlated supply chain stress propagation, policy optimization, and systemic risk quantification while highlighting the exponential computational barriers faced by classical simulation at industrial-scale problem sizes.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces QR-SPPS, a quantum-native framework for assessing correlated failures in multi-tier supply chains, revealing insights that surpass classical models.
AI.motivation: To address the underestimation of correlated cascade failures in traditional supply chain risk models that treat node failures as independent.
AI.method: QR-SPPS utilizes a quantum-native approach with a 40-node supply network encoded in a Hamiltonian, employing VQE and ADAPT-VQE for policy evaluation and cascade failure analysis.
AI.result: The framework demonstrates significant differences in predicted cascade failures compared to classical Monte Carlo methods and enables real-time crisis intervention ranking without repeated optimization.
AI.conclusion: QR-SPPS showcases scalable quantum algorithms for optimized risk quantification and intervention evaluation in supply chains, overcoming classical computational limitations.

title: Analysis of the hidden-charm pentaquark candidates in the $J/ψΣ^*$ mass spectrum via the QCD sum rules
summary: In this work, we study the diquark-diquark-antiquark type $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states in the light-flavor $\mathbf{10}$ representation via the QCD sum rules in details. We exhaust the lowest five-quark configurations and obtain the spectroscopy of the $uusc\bar{c}$ pentaquark states with the quantum numbers $IJ^{P}=1{\frac{1}{2}}^-$, $1{\frac{3}{2}}^-$, $1{\frac{5}{2}}^-$, and suggest to investigate them in the decay chain $Σ_b^+\to P_{cs}^+\,φ\to J/ψΣ^{*+}\, φ$ experimentally.

AI.tldr: This study investigates $uusc ar{c}$ pentaquark states using QCD sum rules, focusing on their properties and suggesting experimental pathways for observation.
AI.motivation: To better understand the properties and configurations of pentaquark states within quantum chromodynamics (QCD).
AI.method: Utilizing QCD sum rules to analyze the lowest five-quark configurations of the $uusc ar{c}$ pentaquark states.
AI.result: Obtained the spectroscopy of various $uusc ar{c}$ pentaquark states with specific quantum numbers.
AI.conclusion: Experimental investigation of the suggested decay chain can provide insights into the properties of these pentaquark states.

title: Intelligence-Guided Adaptive Purification for DDoS-Resilient Quantum Networks: A CUDA-Q based Study
summary: Quantum-repeater networks require adaptive control policies that balance entanglement generation rate, end-to-end fidelity, purification overhead, and memory-induced latency. This tradeoff becomes more complex when the classical control plane is degraded by cyber anomalies or denial-of-service traffic. We develop a CUDA-Q/SeQUeNCe co-simulation workflow for studying adaptive entanglement purification in heterogeneous linear repeater chains. CUDA-Q noisy quantum kernels are used to estimate primitive entanglement purification and swapping behavior, while SeQUeNCe provides an event-layer model for stochastic link generation, waiting-time-dependent memory decay, purification failure, and end-to-end swapping. Under stationary conditions, we compare no purification, local threshold purification, mean-field predictive purification, fixed purification, and a resource-penalized risk-aware predictive policy. In an 8-node chain, the resource-penalized risk-aware controller increases above-target delivery probability relative to fixed purification while reducing latency and purification overhead. We then couple the quantum-network controller to anomaly scores derived from the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 benign-to-SSDP intrusion-detection trace. During the attack period, the attack-unaware controller maintains high raw delivery, but its above-target entanglement delivery falls to 0.098+/-0.007; the IDS-aware resource-adaptive controller switches to more purification-heavy masks and increases above-target delivery to 0.344+/-0.011, closely matching the oracle-aware value of approximately 0.335. These results demonstrate that cyber-state awareness can improve useful quantum-network outcomes by trading raw throughput for fidelity-qualified entanglement delivery.

AI.tldr: The study develops a co-simulation workflow to optimize entanglement purification in quantum-repeater networks, addressing the impact of cyber anomalies. It shows that a resource-adaptive controller improves fidelity and delivery during attacks compared to traditional strategies.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing entanglement purification in quantum networks, especially under conditions of cyber threats that impact classical control systems.
AI.method: A CUDA-Q/SeQUeNCe co-simulation workflow is employed to analyze different purification strategies in 8-node quantum-repeater chains, comparing several adaptive control policies under varying conditions.
AI.result: The resource-penalized risk-aware controller enhances delivery probability and reduces latency and overhead during attacks, outperforming fixed policies. The IDS-aware controller also improves entanglement delivery during cyber attacks.
AI.conclusion: Cyber-state awareness in quantum networking can significantly improve outcomes by enhancing fidelity-qualified entanglement delivery, trading some raw throughput for better performance.

title: Vector mesons leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes and related semi-leptonic decays within QCD sum rules
summary: In this work, we focus on the light vector meson leading-twist longitudinal distribution amplitudes (DAs) $φ^\parallel_{2;V}(x,μ)$ with $V = ρ, K^\ast, φ$. In order to obtain their accurate behaviors, a new scheme of QCD sum rule research with respect to DA suggested in 2021 by us is adopted. With an improved sum rule formula, the $ξ$-moments $\langleξ^n\rangle_{2;V}^\parallel$ up to tenth order are calculated. In which, $\langleξ^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;ρ}=0.225^{+0.013}_{-0.012}$, $\langleξ^1\rangle^\parallel_{2;K^\ast}=-0.0228^{+0.0042}_{-0.0040}$, $\langleξ^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;K^\ast}=0.217^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $\langleξ^2\rangle^\parallel_{2;φ}=0.209^{+0.020}_{-0.020}$, and the corresponding Gegenbauer moments $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;ρ}=0.074^{+0.039}_{-0.036}$, $a^{1;\parallel}_{2;K^\ast}=-0.038^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;K^\ast}=0.050^{+0.020}_{-0.019}$, $a^{2;\parallel}_{2;φ}=0.027^{+0.058}_{-0.058}$ at the scale $μ= 1~{\rm GeV}$, respectively. By fitting those $\langleξ^n\rangle^\parallel_{2;V}(n = 1,2,\cdots,10)$ with the least squares method, the behaviors of leading-twist longitudinal DAs for $ρ, K^\ast, φ$ are determined. Further, we recalculate the transition form factors and branching ratio of the $D\to(ρ,K^\ast)$, $D_s\toφ$ semi-leptonic decay processes.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel approach to calculate the longitudinal distribution amplitudes (DAs) for light vector mesons using an improved QCD sum rule methodology, yielding specific numerical results and enabling further analysis of decay processes.
AI.motivation: To obtain accurate longitudinal distribution amplitudes for light vector mesons: ρ, K*, and φ, crucial for understanding their properties and decay behaviors.
AI.method: A new scheme of QCD sum rules introduced in 2021 is utilized; moments and Gegenbauer coefficients are calculated using least squares fitting of the obtained moments up to tenth order.
AI.result: Calculated moments include \(\langleξ^2\rangle_{2;ρ}=0.225^{+0.013}_{-0.012}\), \(\langleξ^1\rangle_{2;K^*}=-0.0228^{+0.0042}_{-0.0040}\), among others, at the scale of 1 GeV, providing precise parameters for the leading-twist DAs.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully determines the longitudinal DAs for the light vector mesons and recalculates relevant transition form factors and branching ratios for specific semi-leptonic decays.

title: A Hybrid Classical-Quantum Approach for Multi-Constrained Location Optimization Problem
summary: The Maximal Covering Location Problem (MCLP) is an NP-hard Combinatorial Optimization Problem (COP) that aims to determine the optimal facility placements that maximize total coverage. It is characterized by both equality and inequality constraints, which ensure correct coverage but significantly increase the complexity of exploring the solution space as instance size grows. Hybrid quantum-classical approaches might offer a promising alternative to classical optimization methods by enabling the exploration of complex energy landscapes through quantum superposition and probabilistic sampling. In this work, the MCLP is formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, where constraint embedding plays a critical role in solution quality. In particular, Unbalanced Penalization (UP) is employed as an alternative to the Slack Variables (SV) for handling inequality constraints without increasing the number of variables. This study focuses on QAOA and one of its variants, the WS-QAOA, which leverages a biased initial state derived from a continuous relaxation of the problem. Additionally, a linear ramp (LR) parameter schedule is incorporated to reduce optimization complexity. The performance of these techniques is evaluated both individually and in combination, as a function of circuit depth $p$ and problem size. Results show that the combined approach of UP, LR, and WS-QAOA consistently improves solution quality and feasibility metrics, while maintaining robust performance as the problem size increases, highlighting its potential within hybrid quantum-classical optimization frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the Maximal Covering Location Problem (MCLP) using a hybrid quantum-classical approach, proposing a QUBO model that incorporates Unbalanced Penalization and a WS-QAOA variant to enhance solution quality and feasibility.
AI.motivation: To solve the NP-hard MCLP effectively, exploring optimal facility placements under complex constraints remains a significant challenge.
AI.method: The MCLP is formulated as a QUBO model with constraint embedding managed through Unbalanced Penalization (UP) instead of Slack Variables (SV), and optimized using WS-QAOA with a linear ramp schedule.
AI.result: Combining UP, LR, and WS-QAOA leads to improved solution quality and feasibility, with enhanced performance scalability as problem size increases.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method demonstrates significant potential for advancing hybrid quantum-classical optimization techniques in addressing complex combinatorial problems.

title: A Gauge Model for Quasi-Dirac Neutrinos
summary: In a model with $L_μ - L_τ$ Abelian gauge symmetry, anomaly-free chiral fermions, which are Standard Model singlets, are introduced as the origin of right-handed neutrinos. This $\mathsf{U} (1)$ symmetry keeps the right-handed neutrinos Majorana massless. Tiny nonvanishing Dirac masses of neutrinos are due to higher-dimensional operators with natural coupling constants. After gauge symmetry breaking, a quasi-Dirac neutrino scenario naturally appears, and realistic neutrino physics can be produced. Phenomenological and cosmological aspects of the model are discussed.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces anomaly-free chiral fermions linked to right-handed neutrinos via an $L_μ - L_τ$ gauge symmetry, which leads to quasi-Dirac neutrinos and explores their implications.
AI.motivation: To explore a model incorporating right-handed neutrinos while keeping them massless, addressing neutrino mass formation through higher-dimensional operators, and investigating the potential implications for neutrino physics.
AI.method: Theoretical model development based on $L_μ - L_τ$ Abelian gauge symmetry, integrating anomaly-free chiral fermions and employing higher-dimensional operators to generate neutrino masses post gauge symmetry breaking.
AI.result: The emergence of a quasi-Dirac neutrino scenario that aligns with realistic neutrino physics, corroborating the theoretical framework of the model.
AI.conclusion: The model provides a cohesive approach to understanding neutrino mass generation while being consistent with existing phenomenological and cosmological contexts.

title: Number Fluctuations and Entanglement-Spectrum Participation in Monitored Free Fermions
summary: Monitored free-fermion chains show a crossover in entanglement scaling as the measurement rate is increased, from a subextensive weak-monitoring regime to an area law at strong monitoring. I test, using trajectory-resolved correlation-matrix simulations of chains up to $L=96$, whether two diagnostics built from the single-particle entanglement spectrum add practical value: the bipartite particle-number fluctuation $F_A=\sum_kν_k(1-ν_k)$ and a participation-style effective number of entangling modes $\mathcal{M}_A=\exp[-\sum_k w_k\ln w_k]$, with $w_k\proptoν_k(1-ν_k)$. Both quantities track the crossover, decreasing monotonically with measurement probability and losing system-size dependence in the strongly monitored regime. However, at the level of trajectory- and time-averaged steady-state values, $\mathcal{M}$ is almost a deterministic function of $F$: a pooled curve captures 99.7\% of its variance across all measurement rates, so $\mathcal{M}$ carries little independent information in this model. Its main advantage is statistical: the trajectory-to-trajectory coefficient of variation of $\mathcal{M}$ is up to a factor of about 2 smaller than that of the entropy or $F$ at strong monitoring. A model comparison of subsystem scaling at $L=48$--$96$ further shows that, at weak monitoring, a pure logarithmic law is not statistically preferred at these sizes; a small residual quasi-extensive component and a drifting effective logarithmic coefficient remain. I conclude that $F$ is the natural experimentally motivated companion to the entropy, while $\mathcal{M}$ is best viewed as a variance-reduced numerical summary of largely the same information, not an independent diagnostic.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the entanglement scaling properties of monitored free-fermion chains under varying measurement rates, focusing on two diagnostics derived from the entanglement spectrum. It finds that while both diagnostics track a crossover in entanglement scaling, one is more informative than the other.
AI.motivation: To understand how entanglement in monitored free-fermion chains changes with increasing measurement rates and to evaluate the utility of specific diagnostics based on the entanglement spectrum.
AI.method: Trajectory-resolved correlation-matrix simulations of free-fermion chains of length up to 96, examining the bipartite particle-number fluctuation and an effective number of entangling modes across varying measurement probabilities.
AI.result: The diagnostics track the crossover in entanglement scaling effectively, but one is shown to be nearly deterministic with respect to the other, indicating limited independent value. The statistical advantages of each diagnostic were also examined.
AI.conclusion: The bipartite particle-number fluctuation is a more relevant measure for experiments compared to the effective number of entangling modes, which does not provide significant additional information.

title: Quantum numbers of excited $Ξ_c^\prime$ and $Ω_c$ baryons and the $P$-wave $Σ_c$ spectrum
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table, suggestions and comments welcome
summary: Recent precision measurements of excited heavy baryons, combined with systematic theoretical studies, make it possible to resolve the fine structure of their spectra. We calculate the masses and strong-decay properties of the $P$-wave charmed baryons using QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules within heavy quark effective theory (HQET). Although seven states are allowed in each flavor sector, we find that only four $Σ_c$, four $Ξ_c^\prime$, and five $Ω_c$ states are expected to be experimentally resolvable. The similar mass-splitting patterns of $Ξ_c(2882)$, $Ξ_c(2923)$, $Ξ_c(2939)$, and $Ξ_c(2965)$ and of $Ω_c(3000)$, $Ω_c(3050)$, $Ω_c(3066)$, and $Ω_c(3090)$, together with our theoretical results, lead to the successive quantum-number assignments $J^P=1/2^-,3/2^-,3/2^-$, and $5/2^-$. We tentatively interpret $Ω_c(3119)$ as a predominantly $ρ$-mode excitation with $J^P=3/2^-$. We also predict the masses, widths, and dominant decay modes of four resolvable $P$-wave $Σ_c$ states, which may overlap within the observed $Σ_c(2800)$ and $Σ_c(2900)$ structures. Precision spectroscopy of the narrow $Ξ_c$ and $Ω_c$ states thus provides a route to resolving the $P$-wave $Σ_c$ spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the fine structure of excited heavy baryons, predicting which states can be experimentally resolved and providing insights on their properties.
AI.motivation: To resolve the fine structure of the spectra of excited heavy baryons based on recent experimental data and theoretical studies.
AI.method: Utilized QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules within heavy quark effective theory (HQET) to calculate the masses and decay properties of $P$-wave charmed baryons.
AI.result: Identified four $Σ_c$, four $Ξ_c^	ext{'}$, and five $Ω_c$ states as experimentally resolvable, with specific quantum numbers assigned to certain states based on mass-splitting patterns.
AI.conclusion: Precision measurements of narrow $Ξ_c$ and $Ω_c$ states are essential to resolving the $P$-wave $Σ_c$ spectrum, pinpointing new interactions in heavy baryon physics.

title: A Novel Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing (nHQRC) for Phase Transition Detection in Non-Equilibrium Dynamical Systems
summary: The analysis of highly non-linear stochastic data within non-equilibrium dynamical systems requires computational frameworks capable of detecting latent phase transitions before systemic structural breakdowns occur. Traditional Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are frequently bottlenecked by vanishing gradients, the barren plateau problem, and prohibitive training overheads. In this paper, we propose a novel Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing (nHQRC) framework, which bypasses these limitations by employing a frozen, disordered Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM) to project time-dependent stochastic driving forces into an exponentially large Hilbert space. To resolve the physical phase multi-wrapping vulnerabilities present in baseline quantum reservoir models, we introduce a lookahead-free, pre-amplification manifold scaling technique. Multi-qubit configurations are genetically optimized to the "edge of chaos," while quantum state tracking is performed by extracting von Neumann entropy ($S$) and exact mixed-state Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to act as leading entanglement witnesses. Utilizing these quantum triggers as boundary constraints, trajectory predictions are constructed via a generative Stochastic Schrödinger Bridge (SSB) readout. By subjecting the quantum reservoir to an 8-dimensional non-stationary stochastic driving field, the framework significantly improves systemic drift-to-diffusion efficiency ($η$) and actively arrests maximum trajectory decay (MTD) by over 13% compared to standard classical benchmarks. This establishes a robust, $\mathcal{O}(1)$ temporal overhead blueprint for near-term quantum regime detection and macroscopic subsystem stabilization.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing (nHQRC) framework to analyze non-linear stochastic data in non-equilibrium systems, addressing limitations of traditional VQAs and suggesting new methods for trajectory prediction.
AI.motivation: To detect latent phase transitions in non-equilibrium dynamical systems before structural breakdowns and overcome challenges faced by traditional Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs).
AI.method: Utilizes a frozen disordered Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM) to project stochastic forces into a large Hilbert space and introduces a lookahead-free, pre-amplification technique alongside multi-qubit genetic optimization and quantum state tracking through von Neumann entropy and Quantum Fisher Information.
AI.result: The nHQRC framework significantly enhances systemic drift-to-diffusion efficiency and reduces maximum trajectory decay by over 13% compared to classical methods, optimizing quantum reservoir functionalities.
AI.conclusion: This work offers a pioneering $	ext{O}(1)$ temporal overhead structure for near-term quantum applications aimed at phase detection and stabilization of macroscopic subsystems.

title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Architectures for ttH Multilepton Signal Sensitivity
summary: Statistical testing for signal discovery and signal-strength estimation in high-energy physics increasingly relies on machine-learning models trained on simulated data. We present a synthetic dataset for $t\bar t H$ multilepton signal--background classification and perform a systematic evaluation of machine-learning models ranging from the widely used XGBoost for tabular data to LorentzNet, which processes events with built-in Lorentz symmetry. Existing studies often differ in feature definitions, training procedures, and evaluation metrics, making it difficult to isolate the impact of model architecture on performance. To address this, we apply standardized training and hyperparameter-optimization procedures, construct a controlled hierarchy of feature sets, and perform a comprehensive comparison of the models. In addition to the analysis-driven metric of signal-strength uncertainty, we report the commonly used ROC AUC metric and show that under realistically weighted training, it correlates well with the uncertainty-based ranking of models. We further investigate model performance as a function of input feature set, training-set size, and the choice between channel-specific and unified multi-channel training. Our results establish the superiority of Particle Transformer and LorentzNet within the considered setup. We also identify potential avenues for further improvement, including more expressive architectures, joint training across additional analysis channels, and larger simulated datasets. Although this study focuses on a specific Higgs-boson analysis, we expect the main conclusions to generalize to a broader class of searches and measurements at the LHC and HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: The paper evaluates machine-learning models for signal classification in high-energy physics, focusing on a synthetic dataset for $t\bar t H$ events. It standardizes procedures to compare architectures, finding Particle Transformer and LorentzNet to outperform others, and suggests pathways for future improvements.
AI.motivation: The study addresses inconsistencies in existing machine-learning evaluations for high-energy physics by providing a standardized framework to isolate the effects of model architecture on performance metrics.
AI.method: A synthetic dataset was created for $t\bar t H$ signal classification. Standardized training and hyperparameter optimization were applied, alongside a controlled feature hierarchy. Various metrics were used to assess model performance systematically.
AI.result: Particle Transformer and LorentzNet were found to be superior models for the task at hand, with performance metrics indicating a strong correlation between ROC AUC and signal-strength uncertainty.
AI.conclusion: Though focused on a specific analysis, the findings are expected to generalize to other searches and measurements at the LHC and HL-LHC, highlighting areas for further improvement in model training and architecture.

title: The Quantum Correction to Gaussian Information Geometry is the Killing Form of the Symplectic Algebra
summary: On the admissible cone $\mathcal C_Ω=\{Σ\in\mathrm{Sym}^+(2n):Σ+iΩ\ge0\}$ of Gaussian covariance matrices, the classical Bures--Wasserstein transport metric, the Fisher--Rao information metric, and the quantum Bures metric are individually well understood, but their mutual relationship is obscured by the operator equations defining them. Working with the contravariant (dual) metrics, we show that the exact difference between the dual quantum Bures metric and the dual Fisher--Rao metric is independent of the covariance matrix: it is identically the trace form, proportional to the Killing form, of the symplectic algebra $\mathfrak{sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, pulled back through the isomorphism $X\mapstoΩX$. The signature of this form on the Cartan decomposition reproduces the anisotropic stiffening of the quantum metric at the pure-state boundary: it is negative on the compact subalgebra $\mathfrak u(n)$, which carries the divergence, and positive on the noncompact complement. Because the correction is quadratic in the momenta, a no-go lemma shows it cannot arise from minimal coupling to a principal connection. We realize it instead through a Schur complement of a pseudo-Riemannian metric on a phase bundle, whose base reduction is the quantum Bures metric and whose horizontal metric is the classical-limit Fisher--Rao metric. All identities are verified numerically to working precision.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the relationships between different metrics on Gaussian covariance matrices, revealing that the difference between the dual quantum Bures metric and the dual Fisher-Rao metric is constant and related to the symplectic algebra, and introduces a new interpretation using a pseudo-Riemannian metric framework.
AI.motivation: The aim is to clarify the interconnections between the classical Bures–Wasserstein transport metric, Fisher–Rao metric, and quantum Bures metric, which are well-studied but have obscure relationships due to their operator definitions.
AI.method: The authors analyze the dual metrics and demonstrate that the difference between the dual quantum Bures metric and the dual Fisher–Rao metric is a constant trace form from the symplectic algebra, employing a Schur complement for a pseudo-Riemannian metric on a phase bundle.
AI.result: The difference is proven to be independent of the covariance matrix and connects to the properties of the symplectic algebra, showing negative and positive signatures that reflect the anisotropic nature of the quantum metric at the pure-state boundary.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal a stable connection between quantum and classical metrics, offering insights into a pseudo-Riemannian framework that governs these relationships, validated by numerical verification.

title: Hamiltonian Lift of Bures--Wasserstein Covariance Dynamics with a Spectral Floor
summary: Covariance dynamics on the positive-definite cone are commonly described by gradient flows, which encode dissipative relaxation but obscure the underlying phase-space structure. We construct a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian lift of covariance dynamics on Sym$^+_n$ equipped with the Bures--Wasserstein metric. The natural mechanical Lagrangian yields canonical momentum $Π=\tfrac12 L_Σ[\dotΣ]$, where $L_Σ$ is the Lyapunov operator, and explicit Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}(Σ,Π) = 2{\rm tr}(ΠΣΠ)+V(Σ)$. Adding Rayleigh dissipation recovers the Bures--Wasserstein gradient flow in the overdamped limit. For a spectral-floor and trace-control potential, the quadratic fluctuation Hamiltonian around the isotropic equilibrium separates trace and traceless modes; the baseline stiffness diverges as $(s-ν)^{-2}$ as the equilibrium covariance approaches the floor. The construction identifies a conservative parent system for constrained Bures--Wasserstein covariance relaxation and fixes the local stiffness scale induced by the spectral floor.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a framework for understanding covariance dynamics through Hamiltonian mechanics, revealing insights into phase-space structure and dynamics in a positive-definite cone.
AI.motivation: To clarify the underlying phase-space structure of covariance dynamics that traditional gradient flows obscure.
AI.method: A Hamiltonian lift is constructed for the covariance dynamics on Sym$^+_n$ using the Bures-Wasserstein metric, integrating mechanical systems with Rayleigh dissipation.
AI.result: The explicit Hamiltonian allows for separation of modes in the quadratic fluctuation Hamiltonian, with notable divergence of stiffness as equilibrium approaches a spectral floor.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a conservative framework for analyzing Bures-Wasserstein covariance relaxation and identifies the stiffness scale affected by spectral constraints.

title: Wide binaries in ultra-faint dwarf galaxies as a probe of extended dark objects
summary: Wide stellar binaries are sensitive dynamical probes of dark matter substructure. We generalize existing point-mass disruption constraints to spherical extended dark objects and apply the resulting framework to the population of wide-binary candidates identified in the ultra-faint dwarf galaxy Bootes I. We derive 95% confidence limits on the dark matter fraction as a function of the perturber mass, the radius enclosing 90% of the mass, and the density profile, considering Navarro-Frenk-White, r^-3/2, and r^-9/4 models. Sufficiently compact objects converge to the point-mass limit, whereas finite size suppresses binary disruption when the perturber becomes comparable to the relevant encounter and binary scales. The constraints remain sensitive to dark matter fractions well below unity over a broad region of the mass-radius plane and extend to objects substantially larger than those accessible to conventional microlensing searches. As an application, we map the r^-3/2 results onto ultracompact minihalos and derive an illustrative constraint on the primordial curvature power spectrum. Ultra-faint-dwarf wide binaries therefore offer a purely gravitational probe of the abundance of extended dark matter objects and of the small-scale primordial curvature power spectrum.

AI.tldr: This study examines wide stellar binaries in the Bootes I dwarf galaxy to constrain the properties of dark matter through new models of extended dark objects, providing limits on dark matter fractions that inform on primordial fluctuations.
AI.motivation: To explore the effects of extended dark matter objects on the disruption of wide stellar binaries and improve constraints on dark matter characteristics in low-density environments.
